text: We love the convenience of apps like Libby, but "free" for readers doesn't mean free for the library. Every digital checkout carries a hidden maintenance cost. Unlike physical books that sit on shelves for decades, digital licenses are often ephemeral—expiring after a set number of borrows or a specific timeframe. This forces libraries to repeatedly repurchase the same titles just to keep their digital shelves stocked. It creates a relentless cycle of spending that strains budgets already stretched thin between physical collections and vital community programs.

We love the convenience of library apps like Libby, but we often forget that "free" for readers doesn't mean free for the institution. Every digital ebook or audiobook we check out carries a significant hidden maintenance cost. Unlike physical books that last for decades, digital licenses often expire after a set number of borrows. This means libraries must pay repeatedly to renew access just to keep their digital shelves stocked, straining budgets that are already stretched thin between physical collections and vital community programs.
